I understand you have a history of AIDS and are experiencing decreased vision with black spots in your right eye. Can you tell me if you also see a "curtain" or shadow coming down over your vision, or if there is any pain when you move your eye?

REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Understood; given your history of AIDS and the specific symptoms of painless black spots and decreased vision, I am proceeding directly with the diagnostic conclusion. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis.
